correctness.rationale: The admissible panhandle base polytope equals the hypersimplex cut by tail sum at most one. For excluded rank-r vertex with j>=2 tail 1s, the proposed projection has head complement (j-1)/(s-r+j) and retained tail entries 1/j; its support-normal inequality against every feasible y makes it the unique Euclidean projection. The squared residual is (j-1)^2[1/j+1/(s-r+j)]. Strict monotonicity in j gives largest shell, and the residual-variance identity rules out nonvertex farthest points. Equality face is Δ_(j-1,s-r+j) × Δ_(1,j); its dimension is s-r+2j-2. Hypergeometric finite-population CLT plus derivative of g(x)=x+x²/(alpha-rho+x) proves limiting variance in strictly interior proportional regime. An independent new exact rational support-inequality enumerator verified 373 excluded vertices for n<=8; this alone does not prove the all-dimensional or CLT claims.

originality.rationale: Existing panhandle Ehrhart/volume and Schubert matroid results supply polytope definition, not metric distance shells. A published paving-matroid theorem has projection²=1/k+1/(n-hyperplane-size) for a nonbasis inside a rank-(k-1) hyperplane; rank>=3 panhandle has tail parallel 2-circuits and is generally non-paving, so that general paving theorem cannot be specialized to this whole claimed family. Its rank-two overlap is explicitly excluded. Capped-simplex methods do not state this global comparison or hypergeometric law.
